card.title: Thin lenses — lens maker's formula and power of lens

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The lens-maker formula builds 1/f from the index and the two radii. A symmetric convex lens of index 1.50 and radii 20 cm has f = 20 cm. Power is 1/f in metres, so that lens is 5.0 D. The imaging equation is 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A 2 D lens has f = 0.50 m.  ·  μ is the index of the glass relative to the surrounding medium.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: A thin convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges parallel rays to a real focus. A concave lens is thinner in the middle and diverges them. In the Cartesian convention a convex lens in air has positive f.  ·  The lens-maker formula is 1/f = (μ − 1) (1/R1 − 1/R2). The signs of the radii follow the same convention: a surface whose centre is to the right of the surface has a positive radius when light travels to the right.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Lens maker  ·  Dioptre  ·  Convex and concave  ·  Thin-lens equation

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: A convex lens has positive power.  ·  The lens-maker formula uses both radii.  ·  Power in dioptres needs f in metres.  ·  A shorter focal length is a stronger lens.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Lens maker: 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/R₁ − 1/R₂). Power P = 1/f (dioptre, f in metres); lenses add powers in contact.  ·  Refraction at a plane surface (Snell): n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂. Total internal reflection when θ > θ_c, sinθ_c = n₂/n₁ (n₂<n₁).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What is the sign of f for a convex lens in air?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A symmetric double-convex lens has μ = 1.50 and both radii of magnitude 20 cm. Find f and the power.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The lens-maker formula is → A  ·  Power in dioptres uses f in → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: For a symmetric double-convex lens, R1 is positive and R2 is negative, so the two terms add. A higher index or a tighter curve means a shorter focal length.  ·  The power is P = 1/f with f in metres. The unit is the dioptre. A lens of f = 0.25 m has power 4 D. Two thin lenses in contact have powers that add.  ·  The thin-lens equation is 1/v − 1/u = 1/f. A real object has negative u. A real image on the far side has positive v.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ lens maker: 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/r₁ − 1/r₂). power p = 1/f (dioptre, f in metres); lenses add powers in contact..  ·  Power uses metres, not centimetres.  ·  R2 for the second convex surface is negative in this convention.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A concave lens has negative power.  ·  The lens formula is 1/v − 1/u, not the mirror's plus sign.  ·  Convert f to metres before calling the result dioptres.

rows.text: Limit to remember: lens maker: 1/f = (μ − 1)(1/r₁ − 1/r₂). power p = 1/f (dioptre, f in metres); lenses add powers in contact.  ·  The formula assumes a thin lens and paraxial rays.
